That hearing was continued to June 21 so the applicant can supply a drywell schematic, an overflow plan, a remediation plan and securing details. Several other hearings were continued, and certificates of compliance and a tree removal were approved.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none offered.
Asked how plans are enforced if an owner builds beyond the approved plan; chair described certificates of completion and a roof ordered removed.

Read a statement for the Woodlands Village condominium saying it was not properly notified as an abutter of the water district pilot study and asking for postponement; later objected to the tanks, asked for soil testing for PFAS and presented sample data.
Asked about the pilot schedule, PFAS breakthrough testing, leak and freeze risk, and criticised the lack of notification to Woodlands residents.
Said a majority of direct abutters were not notified; asked about drywell depth and capacity, pilot duration and design.
Asked that the notice of intent be updated with specific details before any approval.
Raised the weight of the water tank and a hydrogeology report on lake levels.
Concerned about erosion and runoff to the lake near the tank and drywell.
Asked about alarm systems for malfunctions.
Asked about noise and whether test results would go to the commission.
Asked the engineer for a list of recent PFAS pilot study towns and for a schematic of the system.
Asked who is liable if something goes wrong.
Asked how truck traffic would affect wetlands.
Water district staff asked why they were not told about the site visit.

what_happened.line: In a straw poll, all six voting commissioners favored requiring the water district to file a Request for Determination of Applicability for the Hickory Hills well discharge; no formal vote was taken.
The poll did not waive notice to abutters within 300 feet, after the water district chair asked to limit it.
The Commission opened the notice of intent hearing for 406 Sunset Lane and voted to continue it to January 18 at 7 pm.
The Commission elected a chair, vice chair and clerk, each by roll call with all aye as heard.
It voted to have the town attorney send letters to four landowners about possible encroachments on conservation land.

why_it_matters: A water district discharge into a stream that feeds Hickory Hills Lake will go through the same wetlands filing that residents face, and neighbors within 300 feet are to be notified, which touches the lake's water quality.
The filing and notice costs were argued over as a burden on the district and its ratepayers, so they may reach water bills, though the minutes give no amount.
